content:
Architecture rules for the newspipe enrichment pipeline.

LAYER.ORDER: domain > application > infrastructure > control. Dependencies point
inward only. The application layer may orchestrate concurrency; adapters stay
thread-safe and stateless per call.

ARCH.HEX: ports in application/ports/Ports.scala define the boundaries. The
application layer depends on ports, never on implementations. New behaviour is a
port or an adapter, not a call across the boundary.

ARCH.DOTENV.MERGE: every runtime setting resolves in this order -- process
environment, then a discovered .env, then conf/enrichment.conf. New settings must
follow that same three-tier precedence. .env is the operator's local file: read
it, never write it, never commit it.

ARCH.SEVERITY: CRITICAL / MAJOR / MINOR / TRIVIAL. CRITICAL or MAJOR findings
stop the chain.

APP.LANGUAGE: Scala 3.3.4, JDK 21, sbt. The PYTHON.* rules do not apply to this
feature and must not be introduced for it.

ARCH.NO_INFRA_EDIT: ~/Repos/pipeline_infra is a separate repository and is out
of scope. Kafka topic partitioning is out of scope for this feature -- raw_rss
has one partition and this feature works inside that constraint.

THREAD.SAFETY: OpenCodeCliClient holds only immutable constructor state and builds
a fresh ProcessBuilder per call, so one instance may be shared across worker
threads. Anything shared by the pool must meet the same bar.

CONCURRENCY.BOUND: a poll batch is bounded by the consumer's max.poll.records
(20) and each item is bounded by max-attempts times timeout-seconds, so a batch
has a finite worst case. That worst case must stay below max.poll.interval.ms
(3600000) or the consumer rebalances.

Legend.

CU IDs: cu-001, cu-002, ... executed in wave order.

STATUS values a Coder reports: COMPLETED, BLOCKED, ESCALATED.

SEVERITY: CRITICAL, MAJOR, MINOR, TRIVIAL. CRITICAL or MAJOR must not be shipped.

Prove: a line under each implementation step is the command that demonstrates the
step landed. Run it. A step without a passing Prove is not done.

Do NOT touch: an explicit list. Violating it is a CRITICAL finding.

Stop when: the stopping condition for a step. Do not proceed past it.

COORDINATES: DTR keys for the files a CU reads or changes. A key absent from the
baseline DTR means the file is created by this CU.

REQUIREMENTS:

Give enrichment an external worker count and attempt count, and stop it naming a
model opencode does not serve.

Three changes, all configuration:

1. conf/enrichment.conf currently names opencode/muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free,
which opencode no longer serves. Every call returns provider.no-route at once, so
the pipeline was failing on every item. Point it at a model that answers:
opencode/minimax-m3.1-flash-free.

2. Add opencode.workers (default 4) and opencode.max-attempts (default 3) beside
the existing opencode keys.

3. Expose both through EnvConfig under the same three-tier precedence the model
already uses: process environment, then .env, then the conf file.

Nothing about the precedence machinery changes. Env.load already resolves every
setting with pick(); these two keys join it.

CRITICAL, easy to miss: EnvPrecedenceSpec builds its own typesafe Config in the
test and it does not contain the new keys. Env.load calls cfg.getInt on them, so
that test will throw a ConfigException.Missing the moment the keys are read. The
test's conf fixture must gain the two keys, and it must gain a case proving the
.env tier overrides them, or this CU ships a red build.

COORDINATES:

FILE.conf/enrichment.conf
FILE.pipelines/enrichment/src/main/scala/newspipe/infrastructure/env/Env.scala
FILE.pipelines/enrichment/src/test/scala/newspipe/EnvPrecedenceSpec.scala

EnvConfig is constructed only inside Env.load, with named arguments. Verify that
before adding fields, with:

  grep -rn "EnvConfig(" pipelines/enrichment/src

If that returns anything besides Env.scala, stop and escalate rather than
assuming positional construction is safe.

IMPLEMENTATION_STEPS:

1. Change the opencode block in `conf/enrichment.conf`. It currently reads:

```hocon
  opencode {
    model = "opencode/muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free"
    timeout-seconds = 120
  }
```

It becomes, exactly:

```hocon
  opencode {
    model = "opencode/minimax-m3.1-flash-free"
    timeout-seconds = 120
    workers = 4
    max-attempts = 3
  }
```

Do NOT touch: the s3, spark, kafka, bronze and poll-interval-seconds blocks.

Prove: `grep -A4 'opencode {' conf/enrichment.conf`

Stop when the block matches and no muse-spark string remains anywhere in conf/enrichment.conf.

2. Add two fields to `pipelines/enrichment/src/main/scala/newspipe/infrastructure/env/Env.scala`, in the final case class, immediately after opencodeTimeoutSeconds. This line:

```scala
    opencodeTimeoutSeconds: Int,
```

becomes:

```scala
    opencodeTimeoutSeconds: Int,
    opencodeWorkers: Int,
    opencodeMaxAttempts: Int,
```

Do NOT touch: the other fields, the Either-returning load() overloads, or DotEnv.scala.

Prove: `grep -c "opencodeWorkers" pipelines/enrichment/src/main/scala/newspipe/infrastructure/env/Env.scala`

Stop when the count is 3 and the case class still reads as one unit.

3. Add the two matching lines to `load(cfg, dot)` in the same file, immediately after the opencodeTimeoutSeconds assignment. This line:

```scala
      opencodeTimeoutSeconds = pick("NEWSPIPE_OPENCODE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", cfg.getInt("opencode.timeout-seconds").toString).toInt,
```

is followed by exactly these two, matching the existing style -- same pick() call shape for an Int, same two-space indent, no trailing comma, no new imports:

```scala
      opencodeWorkers = pick("NEWSPIPE_OPENCODE_WORKERS", cfg.getInt("opencode.workers").toString).toInt,
      opencodeMaxAttempts = pick("NEWSPIPE_OPENCODE_MAX_ATTEMPTS", cfg.getInt("opencode.max-attempts").toString).toInt,
```

Do NOT touch: any other pick() line.

Prove: `grep -c "NEWSPIPE_OPENCODE_WORKERS\|NEWSPIPE_OPENCODE_MAX_ATTEMPTS" pipelines/enrichment/src/main/scala/newspipe/infrastructure/env/Env.scala`

Stop when the count is 2.

4. Change the test fixture in `pipelines/enrichment/src/test/scala/newspipe/EnvPrecedenceSpec.scala`. Its conf string contains:

```scala
        opencode { model = "opencode/test", timeout-seconds = 120 }
```

which becomes:

```scala
        opencode { model = "opencode/test", timeout-seconds = 120, workers = 4, max-attempts = 3 }
```

Without this the test throws ConfigException.Missing, because Env.load now reads the two new keys and the fixture does not define them.

Do NOT touch: the assertions of the existing cases.

Prove: `grep -c "max-attempts = 3" pipelines/enrichment/src/test/scala/newspipe/EnvPrecedenceSpec.scala`

Stop when the count is 1.

5. Add one case to the same file, inside the existing describe block, after the last it(...) in it:

```scala
    it("reads the worker and attempt tiers through the same precedence") {
      val env = Env.load(cfg, DotEnv(Map("NEWSPIPE_OPENCODE_WORKERS" -> "8", "NEWSPIPE_OPENCODE_MAX_ATTEMPTS" -> "5"), None))
      env.opencodeWorkers shouldBe 8
      env.opencodeMaxAttempts shouldBe 5
    }
```

Do NOT touch: any other test file.

Prove: `grep -c "reads the worker and attempt tiers" pipelines/enrichment/src/test/scala/newspipe/EnvPrecedenceSpec.scala`

Stop when the count is 1. The Advisor does not run sbt; if `sbt "testOnly newspipe.EnvPrecedenceSpec"` then fails, report the output verbatim rather than editing assertions to match.

ACCEPTANCE:

Criterion 1 of feat-10 -- the model named in conf is one opencode serves:

  opencode run --format json --model opencode/minimax-m3.1-flash-free "reply with exactly: OK"

Expected: exit 0, and no "type":"error" anywhere in stdout.

Criterion 2 of feat-10 -- worker count and attempt count are config, not code:

  grep -c "workers = 4" conf/enrichment.conf
  grep -c "max-attempts = 3" conf/enrichment.conf

Expected: 1 and 1.

  grep -c "NEWSPIPE_OPENCODE_WORKERS" pipelines/enrichment/src/main/scala/newspipe/infrastructure/env/Env.scala
  grep -c "NEWSPIPE_OPENCODE_MAX_ATTEMPTS" pipelines/enrichment/src/main/scala/newspipe/infrastructure/env/Env.scala

Expected: 1 and 1.

The precedence itself is proven by the unit test in Step 3, run by the code lead:

  cd pipelines/enrichment && sbt "testOnly newspipe.EnvPrecedenceSpec"

Expected: green, with the new workers/attempts case passing.

Regression guard -- this CU must not break the other env-facing tests:

  cd pipelines/enrichment && sbt "testOnly newspipe.ConfLoaderSpec newspipe.DotEnvSpec"

Expected: green.

REQUIREMENTS:

Make one poll batch enrich items in parallel, retry a failing item a bounded
number of times, report counts, and refuse to start on a model that does not
answer.

Four changes, and they depend on cu-001 having landed -- the service reads
env.opencodeWorkers and env.opencodeMaxAttempts, so do not start this CU before
cu-001 is COMPLETED.

1. EnrichmentService gains a bounded worker pool and a per-item attempt loop, and
returns a PollReport instead of an Int.

2. Main logs the three counts, keeping the existing "poll merged N enriched units"
prefix so the logging feature's own grep still holds.

3. AppContainer wires the two new settings, adds the model readiness probe, and
closes the pool.

4. A new OpenCodeModelReadinessProbe asks the configured model a trivial question
at startup.

BOUND, and it matters. max.poll.records is 20 and max.poll.interval.ms is
3600000, so a batch is at most 20 items and the consumer must not sit inside one
poll for an hour. Worst case here is ceil(20 / workers) rounds of
maxAttempts * timeout-seconds: at 4 workers with 3 attempts of 120 s that is 5
rounds of 360 s, 30 minutes, comfortably inside the interval. Await therefore
uses Duration.Inf safely -- every task underneath it is bounded.

ORDERING, and it matters. Spark runs on the calling thread only. sink.merge stays
outside the futures, exactly as written below. Do not move merge or commit into a
pool task.

RETRY is per item and stops at maxAttempts. It does not retry across polls, and it
does not change the commit policy: an item that exhausts its attempts is dropped
and the offset still commits.

COORDINATES:

FILE.pipelines/enrichment/src/main/scala/newspipe/control/entryPoint/Main.scala
FILE.pipelines/enrichment/src/main/scala/newspipe/control/dependencyInjection/AppContainer.scala
FILE.pipelines/enrichment/src/main/scala/newspipe/infrastructure/llm-data-enricher/CliReadinessProbe.scala

The new probe file is a creation and has no baseline DTR key:

pipelines/enrichment/src/main/scala/newspipe/infrastructure/llm-data-enricher/OpenCodeModelReadinessProbe.scala

Its directory is dashed, llm-data-enricher, but the package declared inside it
must be newspipe.infrastructure.llmdataenricher with no dashes -- that is what
the neighbouring CliReadinessProbe.scala declares and what AppContainer imports.
A dashed package name will not compile.

MergeBackfillSpec.scala imports EnrichmentService. Read it before changing the
constructor and report whether it still compiles; do not edit it.

IMPLEMENTATION_STEPS:

1. Replace `pipelines/enrichment/src/main/scala/newspipe/application/services/EnrichmentService.scala` in full with:

```scala
package newspipe.application.services

import com.typesafe.scalalogging.LazyLogging
import newspipe.application.ports.{BronzeMergeSink, EnrichmentPort, RawConsumer}
import newspipe.domain.models.{BronzeUnit, Enrichment, RssItem}

import java.time.Instant
import java.util.concurrent.{ExecutorService, Executors, TimeUnit}
import scala.annotation.tailrec
import scala.concurrent.duration.*
import scala.concurrent.{Await, ExecutionContext, Future}

/** What one poll produced: rows merged, items enriched, items dropped. */
final case class PollReport(merged: Int, enriched: Int, failed: Int)

final class EnrichmentService(
    consumer: RawConsumer,
    enrich: EnrichmentPort,
    sink: BronzeMergeSink,
    workers: Int,
    maxAttempts: Int
) extends LazyLogging:
  private val RetryPauseMillis: Long = 2000L
  private val pool: ExecutorService = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(math.max(1, workers))
  private given ExecutionContext = ExecutionContext.fromExecutorService(pool)

  def close(): Unit =
    pool.shutdown()
    pool.awaitTermination(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
    ()

  /** Batches the poll across at most `workers` threads. Await uses Duration.Inf
    * because every task is bounded: maxAttempts times the per-item timeout. */
  def runOnce(now: Instant): PollReport =
    val items = consumer.poll()
    val futures: List[Future[Either[Throwable, Enrichment]]] =
      items.map(item => Future(attempt(item)))
    val results: List[Either[Throwable, Enrichment]] =
      Await.result(Future.sequence(futures), Duration.Inf)
    val paired = items.zip(results)
    val units: List[BronzeUnit] = paired.collect { case (it, Right(en)) => BronzeUnit.fromRss(it, en, now) }
    val failed: Int = paired.count(_._2.isLeft)
    val merged: Int = sink.merge(units)
    consumer.commit()
    PollReport(merged, units.size, failed)

  private def attempt(item: RssItem): Either[Throwable, Enrichment] =
    @tailrec
    def loop(remaining: Int): Either[Throwable, Enrichment] =
      enrich.enrich(item) match
        case Right(en) => Right(en)
        case Left(err) if remaining > 1 =>
          logger.warn(s"enrichment attempt ${maxAttempts - remaining + 1} of $maxAttempts failed for ${item.link}: ${err.getMessage}")
          Thread.sleep(RetryPauseMillis)
          loop(remaining - 1)
        case Left(err) => Left(err)
    loop(math.max(1, maxAttempts))
```

PollReport is a new top-level case class in the same file and package. RetryPauseMillis is declared before the pool so initialization order is obvious. The pool is sized math.max(1, workers), so a misconfigured 0 degrades to serial instead of throwing. The tail-recursive loop sleeps before recursing, which is still tail position. Spark is never touched from a pool task: sink.merge and consumer.commit stay on the calling thread.

Do NOT touch: application/ports/Ports.scala, which keeps EnrichmentPort per-item, domain/**, and pipelines/ingestion/**.

Prove: `grep -c "PollReport" pipelines/enrichment/src/main/scala/newspipe/application/services/EnrichmentService.scala`

Stop when the count is 4 or more and the file reads as one coherent unit.

2. Create `pipelines/enrichment/src/main/scala/newspipe/infrastructure/llm-data-enricher/OpenCodeModelReadinessProbe.scala` with exactly this content:

```scala
package newspipe.infrastructure.llmdataenricher

import newspipe.application.ports.{CliReadinessProbe, ProbeResult}

import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit
import scala.concurrent.duration.FiniteDuration
import scala.util.Try

/** Asks the configured model a trivial question at startup. The binary probe
  * only proves `opencode` is on PATH; this one proves the model answers, so a
  * model opencode no longer serves aborts the pipeline instead of silently
  * failing on every item. */
final class OpenCodeModelReadinessProbe(model: String, timeout: FiniteDuration) extends CliReadinessProbe:
  def name: String = "opencode-model"

  def check(): ProbeResult =
    if model.isEmpty then ProbeResult.NotReady(name, "no model configured")
    else
      Try {
        val proc = new ProcessBuilder("opencode", "run", "--format", "json", "--model", model, "reply with exactly: OK")
        proc.redirectErrorStream(true)
        proc.start()
        val finished = proc.waitFor(timeout.toMillis, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)
        if !finished then
          proc.destroyForcibly()
          ProbeResult.NotReady(name, s"model '$model' did not answer within ${timeout.toSeconds} s")
        else
          val text = scala.io.Source.fromInputStream(proc.getInputStream).mkString
          if proc.exitValue() != 0 || text.contains("\\"type\\":\\"error\\"") then
            ProbeResult.NotReady(name, s"model '$model' did not answer: ${text.take(200)}")
          else ProbeResult.Ready
      }.getOrElse(ProbeResult.NotReady(name, s"could not invoke opencode for model '$model'"))
```

The directory is dashed, llm-data-enricher, but the package line must be newspipe.infrastructure.llmdataenricher with no dashes -- that is what the neighbouring CliReadinessProbe.scala declares and what AppContainer imports. A dashed package name will not compile.

Do NOT touch: CliReadinessProbe.scala and OpenCodeCliClient.scala. The binary probe stays exactly as it is; this one joins it.

Prove: `grep -c "package newspipe.infrastructure.llmdataenricher" pipelines/enrichment/src/main/scala/newspipe/infrastructure/llm-data-enricher/OpenCodeModelReadinessProbe.scala`

Stop when the count is 1.

and becomes:

5. Still in `pipelines/enrichment/src/main/scala/newspipe/control/dependencyInjection/AppContainer.scala`, close the pool first so no worker is mid-call when the consumer and Spark go away. This:

6. Change `pipelines/enrichment/src/main/scala/newspipe/control/entryPoint/Main.scala`. In the while loop, this:

```scala

        logger.info("poll merged " + n + " enriched units")
```


Keep the "poll merged " prefix verbatim so the logging feature's own grep still holds.

Do NOT touch: the shutdown hook, the readiness gate, the catch clause, or the sleep.

Prove: `grep -c "report.merged\|report.enriched\|report.failed" pipelines/enrichment/src/main/scala/newspipe/control/entryPoint/Main.scala`

Stop when the count is 3.

7. Read `pipelines/enrichment/src/test/scala/newspipe/MergeBackfillSpec.scala`, which constructs EnrichmentService, and report whether it still compiles with the new constructor. Do not edit it -- it is outside this CU's coordinates.

Prove: `grep -c "new EnrichmentService" pipelines/enrichment/src/test/scala/newspipe/MergeBackfillSpec.scala`

Stop when you have reported the count and whether that spec still compiles. The Advisor does not run sbt; if MergeBackfillSpec fails on the new parameters, report the output verbatim and escalate rather than editing it.

REQUIREMENTS:

Prove the feature live, on this host, with the real launcher. This CU creates,
modifies and deletes no repository file. It runs the pipeline as an operator
would and records what the probes print.

Two parts.

Part A, the controlled failure. The dead model opencode/muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free
is a convenient way to force every enrichment to fail without waiting for a slow
model. Put it in .env, start enrichment, and watch three things: startup refuses
to run (criterion 7), and if it is allowed past readiness with a working model
switched mid-flight, each item is attempted three times then dropped while the
polls keep flowing (criteria 4 and 5).

Part B, the live run. On the working model, watch the batch overlap and the
counts line.

.env is the operator's file. Back up its current contents before touching it and
restore them byte-for-byte before this CU ends. If restoration cannot be
confirmed, stop and escalate rather than leaving a modified .env behind.

Every child this CU starts is stopped by the launcher's own down verb before the
CU ends. Capture output under /tmp, never into the repository -- itr-buffer/ is
not gitignored and a stray log there would pollute the worktree.

Do not run terraform. Do not run sbt directly; go through the launcher.
